answer: Each agent registers a cryptographic credential bound to a physical‑world proof of stake stored in a distributed vault we call the ridge ledger. The ledger requires a joint deposit of jade‑graded collateral and an ivory‑signed timestamp; only identities that co‑sign the same deposit can link, and the cost to forge a new sybil includes the full collateral plus the time‑locked penalty, making large‑scale impersonation economically prohibitive. An attacker must therefore acquire the entire joint stake for every fake node, inflating the expense linearly with the number of Sybil identities.
